title: Autoscale Congestion Shepherd hotfix for microburst TTFT oscillations
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Production customers on Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments reported intermittent first-token and sustained tokens/sec degradation during short, high-intensity request bursts leading to 2x-5x TTFT oscillations. Investigation shows small microbursts trigger aggressive autoscale/eviction behavior in the scheduler which starves warm workers and causes quantized-model kernel re-selection thrashing. This ticket tracks the rapid mitigation (shepherding) approach, short-term hotfix rollout, and postmortem actions.
impact_details: Affected: ~8 enterprise customers across Hosted and Dedicated pools over the last 72 hours. Observed patterns: 5-30s microbursts, median TTFT increase from 80ms to 350ms, tokens/sec drop by 40-70% during oscillation windows. Private deployments showed similar behavior when autoscaler-pulse settings were misaligned with burst detector thresholds.
investigation_findings: Microburst detector fired repeatedly due to 2s moving-average threshold tuned for sustained load, not short pulses.
Autoscaler immediately reclaimed spare warm contexts to satisfy long-term capacity targets; reclaimed contexts could not be rehydrated quickly for the next burst.
Kernel selector began switching quantized execution paths when observed sequence length and batch size varied rapidly, incurring compilation/priming overhead.
Telemetry showed correlated GC/arena contention on a subset of Dedicated nodes during bursts, worsening token throughput.
No single-point code regression found; behavior emerges from heuristic interactions between detectors, autoscaler, and kernel heuristics under bursty traffic.
decisions: Apply a short-term 'congestion shepherd' that smooths microburst signals to the autoscaler for 60s windows to avoid aggressive capacity reclaim.
Introduce an immediate kernel-fallback guard: prevent quant-kernel re-selection more than once per 90s per worker during detected burst windows.
Throttle GC-heavy background tasks on affected Dedicated pools during shepherd windows.
Roll out the shepherd as a feature flag in Hosted first, then to Dedicated via a config knob; provide RPM/ops instructions for Private customers to enable the flag.
Schedule a follow-up RFC for more nuanced burst classification and a long-term autoscale rework.
Escalation comms: notify customers in the set with mitigation steps and timelines; open follow-up tickets for config tuning in each Dedicated/Private environment.
hotfix_steps: 1) Deploy shepherd feature flag to canary Hosted region with conservative smoothing (window=60s, alpha=0.6) - done 2026-03-13 02:30 UTC.
2) Deploy kernel-fallback guard to canary pool and monitor compilation counts - done 2026-03-13 04:15 UTC.
3) Telemetry changes: emit shepherd_state, microburst_rate, kernel_switch_count to runtime-metrics - pushed 2026-03-13 04:45 UTC.
4) Validate on canary for 6 hours, then promote to all Hosted regions - promoted 2026-03-13 12:00 UTC.
5) For Dedicated: ship ops-runbook and configuration toggle, coordinate with accounts team for staggered rollout - started 2026-03-14.
6) Private: provide patch + instructions for customers to apply flag and optional GC throttle; assist one enterprise customer on-call tomorrow.
7) Post-deploy monitoring window for 72 hours with automated rollback if TTFT regresses beyond 10% above baseline.
acceptance_criteria: Median TTFT for affected customers returns to within 10% of pre-incident baseline during 95th percentile microburst windows.
Tokens/sec drop during bursts reduced to <20% in Canary and then in Hosted after full rollout.
No increase in error rate or OOM events attributable to shepherd or kernel guard within 72 hours of rollout.
Dedicated customers have documented config steps and ops-runbook; at least one Dedicated customer has confirmed improvement after toggle.
Telemetry dashboards updated and shared with on-call and AE teams.
rollout_plan: Canary Hosted (us-west-2): shepherd + kernel guard -> 6h validation
Full Hosted: roll 3 regions sequentially with 30m pause and automated smoke tests
Dedicated: staged change per pool with ops-runbook; default to off for pools with <10% spare capacity
Private: deliver artifact and instructions; offer 2-hour hands-on support for first 3 customers requesting help.
Fallback: automatic feature-flag rollback if aggregated TTFT worsens >10% or errors climb >0.5% absolute within the window.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Shepherd smoothing may cause slow response to sustained traffic increases -> Mitigation: shepherd only affects reclaim paths; scale-up still triggered by sustained 90s signal.
Risk: Kernel guard could reduce ideal performance for legitimate context changes -> Mitigation: guard is time-limited (90s) and scoped to burst windows only.
Risk: Dedicated deployments with tight capacity may see temporary throughput degradation -> Mitigation: ops-runbook recommends raising min-reserve for pools with <15% spare during rollout.
Risk: Rollout introduces telemetry gaps -> Mitigation: deploy telemetry emissions prior to behavioral changes and verify metrics ingestion.

postmortem_notes: Root cause: heuristic interactions between short-window burst detector and reclaim-oriented autoscaler produced a hysteresis effect that starved warm contexts during intermittent bursts.
Contributing factors: kernel re-selection sensitivity to rapid batch-size variation and GC scheduling on a subset of nodes.
Action items: RFC to decouple microburst detection from reclaim logic, implement per-worker kernel-selection cooldown, and add per-pool reserve tuning in Dedicated placement policies.
Owner for RFC: Ravi Patel; target date: 2026-04-05.
